title: Windowed release orchestrator and dependency compatibility adapter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: multiple incidents during near-midnight rollouts and repeated fallout from transitive dependency upgrades motivated a small, focused refactor: introduce a windowed release orchestrator that gates merges to safe roll windows and a dependency-compatibility adapter that runs lightweight ABI/behavior checks before auto-bumping deps. This PR bundles the orchestration glue, a slim preflight runner, and a dep-compat shim intended to be cheap to run in presubmit.
Summary of changes:
1) ci/release-orchestrator: new Go binary (cmd/release-orchestrator) that coordinates merge windows, quiet periods, and graceful drain signals to downstream pipelines.
2) ci/presubmit-hooks: add hook shim to call the dep-compat adapter and short smoke pipeline; hooks are configured as opt-in per-repo via .github/presubmit-config.yaml.
3) tooling/dep-compat: Python adapter that, for a candidate bump, installs the package into an ephemeral venv, runs a curated short test matrix (sanity import, API surface smoke, small model-run smoke where applicable), and emits a compact compatibility report artifact.
4) buildkite/pipeline-stages: reorganize release stages into window-aware lanes and add backoff policy on transient infra failures.
5) docs/ci/release-windows.md and docs/ci/dep-compatibility.md describing behaviors and opt-in migration steps.
Commits (high-level):
- init: release-orchestrator main loop and config parsing
- add: presubmit hook wiring and config schema
- add: dep-compat adapter v0 with import+api smoke checks
- refactor: pipeline stage definitions and backoff policy
- fix: avoid deadlock on drain sequence (race condition fix)
- test: unit/integration harness for the adapter
- docs: usage & migration notes
Changed areas (high-level file list):
- cmd/release-orchestrator/main.go
- ci/hooks/presubmit_runner.go
- tooling/dep_compat/checker.py
- .github/presubmit-config.yaml (new, small opt-in map)
- buildkite/release-pipelines.yml
- docs/ci/release-windows.md
- docs/ci/dep-compatibility.md
- scripts/ci/fixtures/dep-compat-sample
- Makefile entries and CI job templates
Notes on approach and tradeoffs: The orchestrator enforces wall-clock windows defined in org-level config and per-repo overrides. It is intentionally conservative: default rollout windows are UTC 14:00-21:00 but can be narrowed by security or compliance labels. The dep-compat adapter is intentionally lightweight: it is not a full test runner, but a fast preflight that detects common breaking changes surfaced by import/name errors, changed call signatures (via a thin reflection/checklist), and model-based smoke runs when present. We accept occasional false-positives and tuned to allow quick follow-ups; false negatives are minimized by keeping the test matrix aligned with critical integration points.

Review conversation (condensed into single string): Ethan Patel: "Can orchestrator handle multi-tenant pipelines where multiple repos try to claim the same window?" Author (Maya): "Yes, orchestrator uses a lightweight lease in Dynamo (ci-lease table) and will serialize ownership; added retries and jitter to reduce contention." Rosa Kim: "Dep-compat adapter looks good but I'm worried about test flakiness for model smoke runs." Author: "Adapter will skip model smoke by default unless repo opt-in flag present; model smoke uses cached small models and a 10s timeout — documented in dep-compatibility.md." Liam O'Connor: "Need telemetry hooks for rollout failures and backoff counts." Author: "Added metrics (release_window_claim, backoff_attempts, compat_check_result) emitted to statsd; dashboards are in observability-pack PR follow-up."
Requested changes and responses:
- request: make presubmit-config opt-in per default -> addressed by defaulting to false and adding migration guide.
- request: enforce max runtime for adapter jobs -> added 120s hard cap and graceful cancellation path.
- request: better error messages for compatibility reports -> added compact JSON report with human-friendly summary lines.
CI summary: initial runs showed a failing unit test (race in drain handling) and a lint warning in checker.py. Both fixed in follow-up commits; final CI status green: unit tests 120/120, integration smoke 12/12, linters pass, pipeline deployment dry-run passed.
Release notes: "Introduce windowed release orchestrator to schedule merges into defined rollout windows and add a lightweight dependency compatibility adapter for preflight checks on automatic upgrades. Opt-in per repo via .github/presubmit-config.yaml. See docs/ci/release-windows.md and docs/ci/dep-compatibility.md for migration steps."
Rollout plan: staged rollout across infra repos first (ark, infra-config), then core runtime (redwood) opt-in, followed by SDKs.
Breaking change: "false" (not a breaking API change).
Files changed count and delta provided above.
Follow-ups: add an automated dashboard import for the new metrics, a cross-repo adoption tracker script, and extend dep-compat checks to run on scheduled nightly bump candidates to reduce burstiness.
Merged via squash on 2025-11-08 after approvals from Ethan, Rosa, and Liam.
